note.p: Lisa Tutle writes: Jane Wells Webb was born 19 August 1807 in Warwickshire. Her father died, leaving her an orphan, in 1824, and she decided to try to support herself as a writer, moving to London in 1826, where she may have lived for a time in the household of the artist John Martin. I don't know how her connection to the Martins came about but their son, Leopold, wrote that his mother had been almost like a mother to Jane, who was one of several young female writers in whom she took a close personal interest. (Another was Emma Roberts; very likely the "Miss Roberts" from the entry dated 24 March 1834.) In 1827 Jane Webb's first novel was published: The Mummy! A Tale of the Twenty-Second Century. It was reprinted the following year (both times anonymously) and then in 1829 the three-volume Stories of a Bride as "by the authoress of The Mummy."

In February 1830 she met the horticulturist John Claudius Loudon, they were married in September and she abandoned fiction writing for helping her husband with his work, and writing (and, later illustrating) books about gardening, such as Gardening for Ladies (1840) which were extremely popular. She died 13 July 1858. I hope that's of interest. More about Mrs Loudon can be found in a 1961 biography by Bea Howe, Lady With Green Fingers)
